run: what the reference recogniser's settings are worth, measured after a user reported incomplete transcription
why: On 2026-09-21 the user reported two things from using the app: the reference transcript came back incomplete, and a rendered sentence was read with an ezafe nobody wrote. This run answers the first, on this Mac, against transcripts the corpus already carries
what_was_measured: 12 development clips with their corpus transcripts, transcribed by voiceclone's own ASR engine at the configured settings; CER and WER computed with this project's own normalisation (whitespace dropped, harakat folded)

vad_filter_off.note: the first suspect, and the wrong one: turning it off is 3.5 CER points worse

large_v3.note: 0.1 CER points, inside the noise of 12 clips, for 77 times the time on this Mac

decision: nothing changes. faster-whisper large-v3-turbo with the VAD filter on is both the most accurate and, by a factor of 77, the fastest of the three settings tried
the_real_cause_of_incomplete: the preprocessing keeps a window of about 11 s - what the engine is conditioned on - and the transcript describes that window, not the uploaded file. On a 30 s upload that reads exactly like a transcription that stopped early. It is deliberate: a transcript of the whole file would not match the audio the engine hears, which is the failure this project already fixed once. What was missing was saying so, and `a40801f` now prints which seconds the transcript covers, next to the transcript
what_is_left: about 9% CER on crowd-recorded Persian is this recogniser's practical ceiling here, not a setting. The transcript box is editable and the engine conditions on what it holds, so correcting a word by hand is the one thing that reliably improves a render
